items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen in walks of 10 to 19 minutes. If you take insulin or a sulfonylurea, ask your care team about low sugar before adding walks after meals.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Having dinner before 8 pm is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, as sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners. You've been having dinner before 8 pm, and it's a good idea to keep doing that.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You've been averaging an overnight fast of 15.5 hours, which is a good habit to keep. In a study, adding an overnight fast to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points compared with coaching alone.
